outcome: No progress on the Zariski-Lipman conjecture itself was found in the window; the only post-window items are a Lean formalization tracking issue that explicitly lists the statement as still open, and an October 2025 paper that uses already-established (pre-2024) special cases of the conjecture as a tool rather than extending its scope.

ai.basis_quote: Created by AI, reviewed and edited by me.

summary: I searched extensively for any post-26-January-2024 progress on the Zariski-Lipman conjecture (that a complex/perfect-field variety with locally free module of derivations must be smooth) and found none. All substantive special-case results predate the window: complete intersections (Källström), log canonical spaces (Druel 2013; Heuver 2015), normal algebraic surfaces (Biswas et al. 2014), low-genus surface singularities (Graf 2018; Bergner–Graf 2019), toric varieties (Tipler, arXiv:2202.02109, Feb 2022), and the positive-characteristic counterexample/violation results (arXiv:2201.06646, Jan 2022) are all 2022 or earlier. Two items surfaced in the window: (1) a January 2026 GitHub issue (google-deepmind/formal-conjectures #1822) proposing to formalize the conjecture's *statement* in Lean for a benchmark repository — the issue itself says 'Created by AI, reviewed and edited by me,' meaning an AI system (per formal-conjectures' own convention, an LLM) drafted the issue text, which a human then reviewed; this is not mathematical progress, just a benchmark-tracking issue for an open statement, so I coded it formalisation_only with ai_role none (the AI's contribution is tracking/drafting an issue, not producing mathematics). It is also open/unstarted (Formalizability Rating 4/5, blocked on missing mathlib infrastructure), so no proof or even formalization exists yet. (2) arXiv:2510.07607 ('The blow-up of a singularity at the module of derivations,' Barajas–Chávez-Martínez–Romano-Velázquez, submitted October 2025), which studies resolving singularities via blow-ups of the derivation module and explicitly invokes the Zariski-Lipman conjecture as a known true statement in the log-canonical/rational-singularity cases (already settled by Druel and others pre-2024) to conclude smoothness after blow-up. It does not extend the conjecture's proven scope to any new case — it is downstream applied use of prior results, so under the scope rule (§3.1) it does not count as a change to this problem. No expert digestion (Tao's blog, Quanta, survey), no new arXiv preprint proving a new case or a new counterexample, and no AI-generated or AI-assisted proof of any part of the conjecture was found. I judge this a genuine 'nothing happened' case rather than a search failure.
competing_reading: One could argue the October 2025 blow-up paper's Corollary 2.4/Theorem 3.5 results (resolving curve and log-canonical surface singularities via iterated derivation-module blow-ups) constitute 'progress' adjacent to the conjecture's spirit, since they deepen understanding of when the derivation module's freeness controls smoothness. But the paper does not settle any new case of the conjecture itself (it relies on, rather than extends, the log-canonical/rational cases already proved by Druel in 2013), so under the scope rule this is a related problem (resolution of singularities via a different construction) rather than a case of Zariski-Lipman, and I classified it as no_change_found.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement proving the conjecture in a new class of varieties not already covered pre-2024 (e.g., general normal surface singularities beyond the pg-g-b≤2 bound, or higher-dimensional cases beyond complete intersections and toric varieties), or a full general proof/disproof, or an expert survey/blog explicitly stating new movement since January 2024.
